findings.title: Action, disposition, and a traversed path
findings.claim: Each person's ongoing action proceeds according to a personal way, while the Lord's comparison concerns who is better guided on a path. Wider contacts make this relation visible as a characteristic action, a pattern that can channel conduct, and a bearing measured against a traversable route; behavior can disclose and reinforce a pattern without making it a verdict of guidance.
findings.mechanism: The focus pairs its distributive person and ongoing act with شَاكِلَتِهِۦ, then places the Lord's comparison in أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا. The supplied connection to 11:93 has people act from their standing while outcomes expose their stance; 43:22 gives inherited tracks as one concrete course; 67:22 compares bodily bearing with a straight path; and 91:7-8 places moral capacities within a fashioned self. These independent contacts turn an isolated deed into a patterned course whose relation to guidance remains separately evaluated. The 38:58 contact adds only a bounded type/likeness analogy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how action makes a personal pattern observable and why guidedness involves the course a person actually follows, while the focus leaves the comparison with the Lord.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains intact: each acts according to a personal way, and the Lord knows better who is guided along a path. The wider parallels do not decide whether that way is innate, acquired, inherited, or morally fixed. The 38:58 likeness, the 43:22 inherited-track contact, and the work-aptitude facet are bounded analogies; target morphology is not supplied, and none settles a person's final standing.
